assertions_summary.name: memwatch_armed
assertions_summary.actual: ready-file ARMED (pid/pgid/start-ticks authenticated by 01_memwatch.sh); run.log distinguishes ARM REQUESTED from memwatch.log's ARMED line

assertions_summary.name: server_ready
assertions_summary.actual: /v1/models 200 on first poll after memwatch arm-wait (streaming startup maps only the 0.99 GiB token-embedding span); wall-clock timestamps in run.log

assertions_summary.name: o_direct_fd
assertions_summary.expected: at least one open engine fd on the GGUF carries O_DIRECT (aarch64 flag bit octal 0200000) in /proc/<pid>/fdinfo
assertions_summary.actual: 1 of 2 gguf fds has O_DIRECT: fd 34 flags 0600000 = O_LARGEFILE|O_DIRECT (streaming fd); fd 4 flags 0400000 (non-direct header fd) — fdinfo.txt

assertions_summary.name: byte_identical
assertions_summary.expected: temp-0 seed-42 committed fixture, extracted text bytes equal across two consecutive requests

assertions_summary.name: read_bytes_growth_run1
assertions_summary.expected: >= 2 GiB via /proc/<pid>/io during request 1 (O_DIRECT reads bypass page cache, so read_bytes is disk-real)

assertions_summary.name: zero_cuda_stubs
assertions_summary.expected: 0 'CUDA stub called' lines in UNFILTERED server.log

assertions_summary.name: streaming_engaged
assertions_summary.actual: 'cuda SSD streaming total expert budget 16.00 GiB = 3.38 GiB prefill headroom + 12.62 GiB dynamic cache (1915 experts, 6.75 MiB each)' + 'SSD streaming initial cuda model map restricted to token embedding (1 spans, 0.99 GiB tensor span)'

assertions_summary.name: memwatch_no_breach
assertions_summary.actual: 0 breach lines; min sampled MemAvailable 86.72 GiB vs 10 GiB line; ARMED->DISARMED bracket authenticated

observations: Request 2 read 83.90 GB vs request 1's 84.59 GB — 0.8% less. No evidence of meaningful expert-cache persistence across requests on CUDA at this pin; consistent with the source finding that the persistent-cache APIs are no-ops. This is the G4a work item.

Whole-request effective storage throughput ~3.5 GB/s (84.6 GB / 24 s, prefill+decode combined) vs 10.7 GB/s sequential NVMe — selected-expert reads do not reach sequential bandwidth, as predicted in the plan doc.

waivers.criterion: prod stopped for a bounded window, then restored and verified (tailnet 401 + warm probe < 2 s)
waivers.reasoning: Prod was found already down before G1 began: ds4 v0.4.2 received a clean 'shutdown requested' 2026-07-23 21:34 EDT (ds4-server.log) with a clean memwatch DISARM; a llama.cpp engine then served until a clean 'cleaning up before exit' 2026-07-24 09:36 EDT. No crash, no OOM (journal clean), no reboot (uptime 8 days). The user directive for this work authorizes keeping DeepSeek down until GLM is verified ('you may shut down the current deepseek model running/do whatever else you need'). Auth chain observed intact during the window (dsv4-authhelper + caddy units active; :8010 returned 401 at 11:36 EDT — session transcript; not re-captured as raw G1 evidence). Full DSV4 restore + warm-probe verification is deferred to G5, whose round-trip gate proves it end-to-end. Residual risk disclosed: production health is NOT established by G1.

scope_note: G1 proves the streaming MACHINERY on the DeepSeek path only. It proves nothing about GLM-5.2 (G3), nothing about useful throughput (~1.3 tok/s effective here), and nothing about cache effectiveness (explicitly absent, see observations).
